subject: person sitting alone
title: Left Alone With Their Thoughts, 67% of Men Chose an Electric Shock

scenes.text: Most men would rather be shocked than sit and think.
In 2014, psychologists left people alone in a bare room for 15 minutes, with nothing to do but think.
There was one button. It gave them an electric shock.
They had felt it earlier, and three quarters said they'd pay money never to feel it again.
Then the door closed. 67 percent of the men pressed it anyway. So did a quarter of the women.
One man shocked himself 190 times. Fifteen minutes with your own mind: could you do it?

description:
Left alone with their thoughts for 15 minutes, most men chose to give themselves an electric shock.
In a 2014 study in Science led by Timothy Wilson of the University of Virginia, volunteers first felt an electric shock, and three quarters said they would pay not to feel it again. They were then left alone in a sparsely furnished room with nothing to do but think, and a button that delivered the same shock. 67 percent of the men and 25 percent of the women pressed it at least once. One man pressed it 190 times; he was left out of the averages. In earlier rounds without the button, nearly half of 409 participants said they did not enjoy simply sitting and thinking.
Could you sit for 15 minutes with no phone? Comment below.
first_comment: Those who pressed the button gave themselves about 1.5 shocks on average in 15 minutes. Would you have pressed it?
